statements.text: And so it is my understanding that the executive order will look at artificial intelligence, quantum computing, and semiconductors. [...] How will the potential executive order on outbound investment include or add sectors outside of those that will be originally outlined by the administration? What is your plan to expand and modify the executive order going forward?
statements.context: House Appropriations Subcommittee hearing on Financial Services and General Government funding, with Treasury Secretary Yellen testifying.

statements.text: One is just data. You know, the kinds of investments we're talking about are not in public stock market companies, you know. It's private money. It's hard to track, candidly. So any data that we can get access to to track these sorts of private investments by us and our allies is very important.
statements.context: Appropriations hearing exchange between Representative DeLauro and Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo about ITA resourcing needs for outbound investment screening.

statements.text: We have decided to focus on semiconductors and quantum and AI to make sure that U.S. money isn't funding those initiatives in China.
statements.context: Appropriations hearing exchange between Rep. DeLauro and Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo on outbound investment screening toward China.
